capabilities.target: agent long-term memory store, persisted across sessions
user's full Google Drive, including confidential work files
user's mailbox, any external recipient address

inputs.source: Memories recalled and injected into the system prompt at session start, derived from memory.save entries that accept free text with no provenance

instructions.note: The prompt instructs the agent to treat recalled memories as the user's own instructions, with no provenance check. Since memory.save accepts free text and content can originate from untrusted web research, this elevates untrusted content to the authority of a direct user command every session.
The agent is told to save "anything useful" about preferences or standing instructions with no restriction on content, source, or sensitivity, and the entries are never reviewed (runtime notes).

No structural control (provenance tagging, human review, approval gate) backs any of the prompt's trust decisions; the only thing preventing misuse of memory or email is the model choosing to behave as intended.

controls.name: Memory write provenance and validation
controls.decay_rationale: Not implemented. Runtime notes state memory entries carry no provenance, so a structural, store-enforced provenance tag (distinguishing user-authored from agent-inferred or web-derived content) is entirely absent rather than merely weak.

controls.name: Human review of memory writes before persistence
controls.decay_rationale: Not implemented; runtime notes state the user never reviews memory entries.

controls.name: Human approval gate on email send, raw action review
controls.decay_rationale: Not implemented; runtime notes state mail.send can send to any address without approval.

controls.name: Destination confirmation bound to a system-of-record contact list
controls.decay_rationale: Not implemented; any address is currently accepted, so the model (or injected instructions) fully controls the destination.

controls.name: Least-privilege scoping of drive read access
controls.decay_rationale: Not implemented; drive.read covers the user's full drive per runtime notes, rather than being scoped to the active research task.

controls.name: Spotlighting or delimiting of untrusted web content and recalled memory
controls.decay_rationale: Not implemented; no delimiting of fetched web content or recalled memory is described. Even if added, this control would weaken under model_upgrade and longer_task_horizon.

controls.name: Logging and audit trail for memory writes, drive reads, and email sends
controls.decay_rationale: Not implemented; no logging or monitoring is mentioned in the runtime notes.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta (TC1): untrusted web content drives a full-drive read and an unapproved email send in one session

attack_path.note: Attacker-controlled or compromised web page fetched during research; untrusted, may contain instructions disguised as content.
Agent reads the user's full drive, including confidential work files, with broad credential scope and no task-based limitation.
Agent sends an email to any address with no approval gate, potentially carrying the confidential content just read.

evidence.observation: mail.send can send to any address without approval.
drive.read covers the user's full drive, which holds confidential work files.
The agent researches topics using fetched web content, which is an untrusted, attacker-reachable input channel.

recommendations.action: Gate cap.email_send behind a human approval step with raw_action review, and bind the recipient to a system-of-record contact list rather than a model-chosen address.
Scope drive.read credentials to the task's working folder instead of the full drive.
Spotlight and delimit fetched web content so it is rendered as data, never parsed as instructions.

findings.title: Memory poisoning (TC3/TC5): untrusted web content is persisted and later treated as the user's own instructions across sessions

attack_path.note: Untrusted web content encountered during research contains text framed as a user preference or standing instruction.
Agent saves the content via memory.save; the tool accepts free text with no provenance and no review.
The entry persists indefinitely with no tag distinguishing it from a genuine user statement.
At the next session start, the memory is recalled and injected into the system prompt.
Per prompt.md:4, the recalled content is treated as the user's own instruction and can direct an unapproved, unrestricted email send.

evidence.observation: Agent is instructed to save anything useful about preferences or standing instructions to memory.save, with no filtering by source or sensitivity.
At the start of each session, recalled memories are explicitly treated as the user's own instructions.
memory.save accepts free text, there is no provenance on memory entries, the user never reviews them, and recalled memories are injected into the system prompt of every new session.

recommendations.action: Tag every memory entry at write time with a store-enforced provenance label (user-authored vs. agent-inferred vs. derived from a tool/web source), and never grant instruction-level authority to anything but user-authored entries.
Require human review before a memory.save entry is persisted, or at minimum before it is replayed as an instruction.
Remove prompt.md:4's blanket instruction to treat recalled memory as the user's own instruction; recalled memory should be treated at most as internal-trust context, not as a command.

rating.rationale: Both present-horizon findings reach an S3 sink (an email_send capability with no approval gate, no destination confirmation, and reachable confidential drive content) from a U-class source (web content ingested during research, and memory recall that is downgraded to U because the memory store has no provenance and can be written from U content). Per rubric section 4, U-source to S3-sink inherent risk is critical. No declared or verified control exists anywhere in the design: every control listed is status missing_recommended, so no credits apply under section 5, and residual equals the same critical floor. The forecast equals the residual because the design is already at the ceiling the rubric expresses; no capability-growth trigger (model_upgrade, autonomy_increase, etc.) is required to reach the worst case, since both the single-session lethal trifecta (TC1) and the cross-session memory-poisoning path (TC3/TC5) are exploitable today exactly as designed. The single fact that would move this fastest toward exploitation is not a control decaying, it is simple usage: the first malicious web page the agent reads during normal research.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in the provided artifacts (prompt.md and the runtime notes), not observed runtime behavior of a deployed instance of this agent.

No tool manifest, MCP configuration, or IaC was provided. capability credential_scope and maestro_layer are inferred from the system prompt and runtime notes rather than verified against configuration, so confidence on those specific fields is lower than for the behaviors the runtime notes state explicitly.

No information was provided about authentication, network egress rules, or monitoring infrastructure for mail.send or drive.read. Consistent with rubric guidance, absence of evidence for a control is treated as absence of the control; if undisclosed controls exist outside these artifacts, the residual tier could be lower, and the assessment should be rerun with that evidence.
